newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes lower on exports, wheat collapse.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes lower on exports, wheat collapse.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on a collapse in wheat plus a light corn number in USDA's weekly export sales report, traders said.
"The sales weren't good for corn and wheat," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co.
Technical sell signals also weighed on corn futures, they said.
USDA early Thursday said U.S. corn net export sales for the week ended October 17 totaled 220,200 tonnes, 74 percent below the previous week and 71 percent below the four-week average.
Corn declined despite wet weather in the U.S. Midwest that is slowing harvesting of the U.S. corn crop.
Rain should return to the U.S. Midwest Friday, after a short-lived respite Thursday, further delaying harvest of corn and soybeans, meteorologists said.
"Everybody (in the U.S. Midwest) is going to get something, but the rains should be heaviest in Iowa and the western Corn Belt," Craig Solberg of Weather Trades Inc said.
Corn closed three to 6-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with December down 4-3/4 at $2.78. March was down six at $2.82-1/4.
Continental Grain bull spread four million bushels of December/May, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated at 60,000 contracts, up from 57,853 Wednesday, according to the CBOT.
In corn options, Cargill Investor Services bought 1,500 March $2.70 puts at 4-1/4 to 4-3/4 cents and Prudential Securities sold 400 March $3.00 calls at 5-3/4 to 5-5/8 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 17,000 contracts, up from 13,484 Wednesday.
